div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 15px; margin-left: 18px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 22px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: Azure Entra ID to AI Gateway: the complete agent identity flow

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 43px; margin-left: 18px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: Every element on the path a single agent call takes, from the directory that was synced last night to the provider the gateway finally reaches. Entra ID appears in three places and means something different in each.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 88px; margin-left: 18px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: A — CONTROL PLANE. Runs on a sync schedule, never on the request path.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 408px; height: 1px; padding-top: 121px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
1. Azure Entra ID tenant
Users and security groups. The system of record for who exists and who belongs to what.
Entra's first job of three. Okta and on-premises AD slot in here instead, unchanged downstream.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 408px; height: 1px; padding-top: 121px; margin-left: 508px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
2. Cloud Identity Engine
In Strata Cloud Manager. A cloud directory of type Azure AD, authorised against the tenant.
User Identity Attribute: UPN or Mail. Choose Mail when the UPN is user@tenant.onmicrosoft.com and the real address differs.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 378px; height: 1px; padding-top: 121px; margin-left: 988px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
3. AI Gateway Directory Sync
An administrator maps each CIE group to exactly one AI Gateway workspace. One group, one workspace.
Background sync provisions new members and deprovisions departed ones.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 376px; height: 1px; padding-top: 121px; margin-left: 1438px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
4. Workspace membership
Each synced user is a workspace member holding a workspace role, keyed by the email the directory supplied.
This list is the only thing step 9 compares the token against.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 332px; margin-left: 18px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: B — ONE-OFF CONFIGURATION. Three places, three different Entra objects. None of them is the other.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 568px; height: 1px; padding-top: 365px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
App registration in Entra, for the agent
Gives the agent something to authenticate as. Client credentials for an unattended agent, on-behalf-of when a signed-in person is behind the call.
Entra's second job of three: token issuer.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 568px; height: 1px; padding-top: 365px; margin-left: 648px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Admin Settings → Organisation → Authentication
Paste the JWKS URL, or the static JWKS JSON. A comma-separated list is accepted and the keys are merged.
https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/discovery/v2.0/keys

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 546px; height: 1px; padding-top: 365px; margin-left: 1268px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Gateway environment, hybrid and air-gapped only
JWT_ENABLED=ON
ORGANISATIONS_TO_SYNC=<org>
PORTKEY_CLIENT_AUTH=<token>
JWT_LOCAL_AUTH_DEFAULT_SCOPES=…
Gateway 2.5.0 or higher. Backend v1.13.0 or higher for air-gapped.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 558px; margin-left: 18px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: C — PER REQUEST. One agent call, start to finish.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 798px; height: 1px; padding-top: 593px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
1 · The agent asks Entra for a token
Client credentials for an unattended agent, or on-behalf-of to carry a signed-in person. Nothing about the gateway is involved yet.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 798px; height: 1px; padding-top: 695px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
2 · Entra returns a signed JWT
Header carries alg: RS256, typ: JWT and a kid. Payload carries at minimum iss, aud, sub and exp.
You cannot add gateway-specific claims to a stock Entra token. That is what makes this a Mode B integration.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 798px; height: 1px; padding-top: 819px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
3 · The agent sends the inference call
x-portkey-api-key: <raw JWT> or Authorization: Bearer <JWT>
Do not write the word Bearer inside x-portkey-api-key. That is the single most common setup failure.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 798px; height: 1px; padding-top: 943px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
4 · The gateway decides where to validate
A JWT-shaped token on Cloud goes to the management plane. On hybrid or air-gapped with JWT_ENABLED=ON the data plane verifies it itself and keeps working while the management plane is unreachable.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 798px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1057px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
5 · Signature and header checks against the JWKS
The kid must resolve to a key in the JWKS. alg must be RS256, the RSA key must be 2048-bit or larger, and exp must be in the future. Small clock skew is tolerated.
Every failure here is written to the audit log and returned to the caller as an invalid-key error.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 798px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1187px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
6 · Resolve the organisation and the workspace
Organisation: portkey_oid or organisation_id from the token, otherwise ORGANISATIONS_TO_SYNC.
Workspace: portkey_workspace or workspace_slug from the token, otherwise the first entry in the workspace allowlist, otherwise the organisation default workspace.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 798px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1317px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
7 · Resolve the scopes
From the token's scope string or scopes array, otherwise from JWT_LOCAL_AUTH_DEFAULT_SCOPES. A chat completion needs completions.write. The portkey. prefix is optional.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 798px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1431px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
8 · Read the identity out of the claims
The gateway takes the first claim present, in this order: email_id → sub → uid
That value is what per-user logging and per-user metrics are keyed on.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 806px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1583px; margin-left: 23px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: 9 · One string comparison Does that email match a workspace member from band A, step 4?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 374px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1699px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Match
The call is attributed to that person and inherits their workspace role. Logs, metrics and per-user budgets all resolve to a human being.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 374px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1699px; margin-left: 452px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
No match
The call falls back to a generic workspace service key. It still succeeds. No error is returned, and the only symptom is attribution that quietly stops naming anyone.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 798px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1883px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
10 · Policy, limits and the log record
Workspace usage limits, rate limits, budget policies and guardrails run against whatever identity step 9 settled on. The log entry is written with the same value.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 798px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1997px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
11 · Egress, on a completely different credential
The gateway calls Azure AI Foundry with the credential held in its own provider configuration: an API key, or an Entra service principal or managed identity.
The agent's token never leaves the gateway. Foundry sees the gateway, not the agent, and not the person.
Entra's third job of three.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1660px; margin-left: 261px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #333333; background-color: #ffffff;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; background-color: #ffffff; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: yes

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1660px; margin-left: 591px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #333333; background-color: #ffffff;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; background-color: #ffffff; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: no

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-end; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 556px; margin-left: 856px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #666666; background-color: #ffffff;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; background-color: #ffffff; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: compared against

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 926px; height: 1px; padding-top: 593px; margin-left: 888px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
The three Entra objects, side by side
Source directory (band A). Configured in Strata Cloud Manager, under Cloud Identity Engine. Decides who is a workspace member. Never consulted during a request.
Token issuer (band B, step 1). Configured as an app registration in Entra plus a JWKS URL in the gateway. Consulted on every request.
Egress credential (step 11). Configured on the gateway's Azure provider. The caller never sees it and cannot influence it.
All three can point at the same Entra tenant. They are still three separate configurations, and breaking one does not break the others.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 803px; margin-left: 878px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: What the token can and cannot carry

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 440px; height: 1px; padding-top: 835px; margin-left: 888px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Mode A — you control the issuer
{
"sub": "agent-7",
"email_id": "ana@corp.com",
"portkey_oid": "org_abc",
"portkey_workspace": "ws_ai",
"scope": "completions.write",
"usage_limits": { … },
"rate_limits": { … },
"exp": 1767225600
}
Org, workspace, scopes and limits all travel in the token. Nothing has to be configured on the gateway side.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 440px; height: 1px; padding-top: 835px; margin-left: 1374px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Mode B — a stock Entra token
{
"iss": "https://login.micro…",
"aud": "api://ai-gateway",
"sub": "a1b2c3d4…",
"exp": 1767225600
}
Entra is named in the product documentation as a Mode B case, alongside Okta, Auth0 and Cognito.
Organisation comes from ORGANISATIONS_TO_SYNC, workspace from deployment settings, scopes from the IdP registration or JWT_LOCAL_AUTH_DEFAULT_SCOPES, limits from the workspace.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 926px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1207px; margin-left: 888px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Where step 5 actually runs
AI Gateway Cloud. The management plane validates every token. Nothing to configure beyond the JWKS URL.
Hybrid and air-gapped. Set JWT_ENABLED=ON and the data plane verifies locally, which removes a management-plane round trip from every call and keeps authentication working through a control-plane outage. Leave it off and JWT-shaped tokens go to the management plane as before.
JWKS fetches honour HTTPS_PROXY and TLS_CA, so an egress-restricted gateway can still reach Entra.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 926px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1415px; margin-left: 888px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Failure modes worth knowing before you debug one
HS256 instead of RS256 — rejected, and the error reads like a bad API key rather than a bad algorithm.
Missing or unresolvable kid — Error Verifying JWT token: Signing Key Not Found.
Bearer written inside x-portkey-api-key — send the raw token there, or use the Authorization header instead.
Private key pasted into the JWKS — the JWKS holds public key parameters only.
JWKS URL unreachable — the gateway has to be able to fetch it, which an egress policy can quietly prevent.
Entra omits alg on its JWKS keys — fixed in v2.1.0, which falls back to RS256. Older builds fail here.
Scope missing — a perfectly valid token still gets refused. Entra generally cannot issue completions.write, so JWT_LOCAL_AUTH_DEFAULT_SCOPES is usually required.
Empty identity attribute — a user whose chosen UPN or Mail attribute is blank is skipped during CIE sync, silently, and then never matches at step 9.
All invalid-JWT errors land in the audit log, with the token redacted to its first and last few characters.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 926px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1703px; margin-left: 888px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: If none of this is what you wanted An unattended agent with no person behind it has no email to match, so step 9 will always fall through. Give that agent its own workspace service key and name it in x-portkey-metadata, rather than building a token flow that attributes every call to the same generic key.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 926px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1851px; margin-left: 888px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Where identity forwarding stops
Everything above decides what the gateway knows about the caller. None of it reaches the model provider, and only some of it reaches a downstream tool.
MCP Gateway can forward caller identity to an MCP server three ways: a claims header, passing the original bearer token through, or a gateway-signed JWT in a header you name.
Agent Gateway (A2A) has no equivalent. A client authenticates with a gateway API key carrying the agents.invoke scope, and access control is per agent and per skill. Per-user access control for agents is listed as coming soon.
So an A2A call can be attributed, but it cannot carry the caller's identity onward to the agent it invokes.
